openDoors.note: A program or lender review does not guarantee mortgage approval.

lenders.note: Users should compare loan terms, fees, and services; inclusion does not equal an endorsement by this hub.

disbInsurance.name: Homeowners and renters insurance guidance

disbInsurance.desc: Learn what to compare when shopping for homeowners or renters insurance.

ota.desc: Start with the District office focused on tenant rights, education, and advocacy.

housingCode.desc: Learn about District housing-code standards before reporting a condition.

inspection.desc: Review the official process for requesting an inspection of suspected housing-code violations.

vacant.name: Vacant and blighted properties dashboard
vacant.desc: View the District’s public dashboard for vacant and blighted property information.
vacant.note: This is not a sale, rental, or acquisition listing. Confirm property status through official records and do not enter private property.

erap.name: Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) status
erap.desc: Check the official ERAP portal for current status, eligibility information, and available next steps.
erap.note: Appointment availability can pause or change.

rentalAssist.desc: Compare official rental-assistance starting points and current program information.

dcbar.desc: Review legal-help options for DC housing disputes and court-related housing problems.
dcbar.button: Review DC Bar housing legal help

legalAid.name: Housing law help
legalAid.desc: Learn about nonprofit legal assistance for eligible DC tenants facing housing problems.
legalAid.button: Review Legal Aid DC housing help

nlsp.name: Housing law services
nlsp.desc: Review housing-law assistance for eligible DC residents.

oag.name: DC tenant resources
oag.org: Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia (OAG)
oag.desc: Read official tenant-rights information and find appropriate complaint or legal-help pathways.

daclCase.name: Case management for older adults and adults with disabilities
daclCase.org: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
daclCase.desc: Learn about eligibility-based case management, referrals, applications, and follow-up support.

dccil.name: Independent-living services and advocacy
dccil.desc: Explore independent-living advocacy, skills, information, and referrals for people with disabilities.
dccil.button: Explore DC Center for Independent Living services

ddsBlind.name: Services for people who are blind or have low vision
ddsBlind.desc: Review disability-services information for DC residents who are blind or have visual impairments.

veterans.name: Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs
veterans.desc: Find current District resources and navigation support for veterans and military families.
veterans.button: Open the Veterans Affairs resource page

dhsHousing.name: Housing programs for individuals
dhsHousing.desc: Review official housing-program starting points for individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

dash.name: Safe housing and survivor support
dash.desc: Explore safe-housing programs and survivor-centered navigation for people affected by domestic or sexual violence.

cameras.name: Private Security Camera Incentive Program
cameras.org: DC Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG)
cameras.desc: Review the District’s current security-camera rebate and voucher information.
cameras.note: Eligibility, funding, and program availability can change; confirm on the official page.

sfrrp.name: Single Family Residential Rehabilitation Program (SFRRP)
sfrrp.org: DC Department of Housing and Community Development
sfrrp.desc: May fund roof repairs or accessibility changes for qualifying DC owner-occupants.
sfrrp.why: Useful when a homeowner needs larger structural work, such as a ramp, accessible bathroom, stair lift, walkway, or roof repair.
prep: Proof of ownership and primary residence
Household income, mortgage, tax, and insurance records
Physician documentation when accessibility work requires structural changes
sfrrp.status: A 20-year affordability covenant may apply. Do not start work or hire a contractor before approval.
sfrrp.next: Review the eligibility rules, then begin through a current participating community organization.

ems.name: Emergency Mechanical Systems Program
ems.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE)
ems.desc: May repair or replace a failed heating system, central air conditioner, water heater, or chimney liner.
ems.why: A strong starting point when essential mechanical equipment has stopped working and the household meets program rules.
prep: Government identification and household documents
Income or qualifying-benefit proof and utility bills
Ownership or rental, property, and insurance records
ems.status: The EMS program is open and is contacting waitlisted applicants in first-come order. Funding and contractor capacity can change.
ems.next: Use the shared DOEE application before hiring or paying a contractor.

wap.name: Weatherization Assistance Program
wap.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment
wap.desc: Uses a home energy audit to identify approved efficiency and related health-and-safety work.
wap.why: Possible work includes insulation, duct sealing, heating or cooling repairs, air-leak reduction, and other audit-recommended measures.
prep: Photo ID and household Social Security documentation
Income, benefits, bank, and utility records
Mortgage or deed plus homeowner or renter insurance
wap.status: FY2026 WAP openings are delayed. Waitlisted applicants will be contacted. It is not a remodeling or cosmetic-renovation program.
wap.next: Apply for an energy audit and let the audit determine what work may be covered.

drafty.name: Drafty windows and insulation
drafty.desc: There is no standing program that gives every DC homeowner free replacement windows.
drafty.why: Weatherization may address drafts through insulation, air sealing, and approved repairs. Window or door work is possible only when the audit, rules, scope, and funding support it.
prep: Notes or photos showing drafts, leaks, or damage
The regular Weatherization household documents
Access for the program’s home energy audit
drafty.status: New windows are not guaranteed. Do not hire a contractor based on an advertisement claiming automatic free DC windows.
drafty.next: Request a Weatherization energy audit instead of applying for a “free window” giveaway.

electrification.name: Affordable home electrification and residential rebates
electrification.org: DOEE and DC Sustainable Energy Utility (DCSEU)
electrification.desc: Offers income-qualified electrification help and separate equipment rebates available at different income levels.
electrification.why: May reduce the cost of heat pumps, water heating, cooking equipment, appliances, and other eligible electric upgrades.
prep: DC address and utility information
Household income for income-qualified programs
Equipment details, contractor quote, or purchase proof as required
electrification.status: FY2026 rebates may change after September 30. Some programs approve work first; others reimburse after purchase.
electrification.next: Check the current offer and approval order before buying equipment.

energyBill.name: Energy bill assistance
energyBill.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment
energyBill.desc: LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program) and the Utility Discount Program may reduce energy costs for qualifying DC households.
energyBill.why: Useful while a household is waiting for repairs or needs help keeping utility service affordable.
prep: Photo ID and household documents
Current income information
Recent utility bills and proof of address
energyBill.status: As of September 14, 2026, applications are closed until the new fiscal year begins October 1, 2026.
energyBill.next: Check the official page again when the new application cycle opens.

solar.name: Solar for All
solar.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment / DCSEU
solar.desc: May provide rooftop solar for qualifying households or Community Solar savings without panels on the home.
solar.why: Community Solar can be useful when a roof is shaded, unsuitable, rented, or unavailable for an installation.
prep: Current income information
DC address and Pepco account
Ownership, roof, and electrical information for rooftop projects
solar.status: FY2026 single-family rooftop funding is limited. An application does not guarantee funding. Recheck after the September 30 fiscal-year change.
solar.next: Compare the rooftop and Community Solar routes before choosing one.

riversmart.name: RiverSmart Homes
riversmart.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment
riversmart.desc: Offers a free stormwater audit and several yard improvements that reduce runoff.
riversmart.why: May include rain barrels, rain gardens, native landscaping, permeable surfaces, and free shade trees.
prep: DC property address
Owner permission when the applicant rents
Access for the stormwater audit
riversmart.status: Not every improvement is free. Some require a copay or reimbursement, and some are limited by location and site conditions.
riversmart.next: Begin with the free property audit to learn which options fit the site.

casey.name: Free trees and tree rebates
casey.desc: Provides free tree planting at suitable DC properties and a separate rebate for qualifying tree purchases.
casey.why: A tree may provide shade, reduce runoff, cool the property, and improve the yard without the full planting cost.
prep: DC property address
Owner permission
A suitable planting location and agreement to care for the tree
casey.status: Tree type, number, and placement depend on the property. Rebate purchases must follow current species and receipt rules.
casey.next: Request a site review before choosing the tree or planting location.

safeHome.name: Safe at Home
safeHome.org: DC Department of Aging and Community Living
safeHome.desc: Provides preventive home adaptations for eligible older adults and adults with disabilities.
safeHome.why: May help with grab bars, handrails, bathtub cuts, shower seats, stair lifts, and other changes that reduce falls.
prep: Proof of DC residence
Proof of age or disability
Household income and ownership or rental information
safeHome.status: Current published eligibility covers residents age 60+ or adults age 18+ with disabilities.
safeHome.next: Check Safe at Home before paying for accessibility work yourself.

eaas.name: Environmental Accessibility Adaptation Services
eaas.desc: A Medicaid long-term-services pathway that may authorize home accessibility adaptations in an eligible adult’s care plan.
eaas.why: May help an adult who needs safety changes such as rails, shower equipment, or a lift as part of approved Medicaid services.
prep: Current Medicaid information
Clinical and functional assessment
Care plan and information about the home
eaas.status: The public explainer contains older financial figures. Confirm current rules with the Medicaid care manager before relying on exact limits.
eaas.next: Ask the person’s Medicaid care manager whether home adaptations can be assessed.

leadPipe.name: Lead Pipe Replacement Assistance
leadPipe.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment / DC Water
leadPipe.desc: May cover approved replacement of a qualifying private-side lead, galvanized, or brass water-service line.
leadPipe.why: The DC Water service-line map can show whether the property may fit the assistance route.
prep: Recent DC Water bill
Owner photo identification
Proof of ownership and the service-line map result
leadPipe.status: This is not reimbursement. Do not hire a contractor or pay a deposit before written approval, and use an approved contractor.
leadPipe.next: Check the service-line map, then follow the assistance-program approval steps.

leadReduction.name: Lead Reduction Program
leadReduction.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment
leadReduction.desc: May identify and reduce lead-paint hazards in qualifying pre-1978 homes connected to a young child.
leadReduction.why: Designed for eligible homes where a child under 6 lives or visits frequently and lead hazards may be present.
prep: Child’s birth certificate and household documents
Income, asset, ownership, and insurance records
Any existing lead inspection or hazard reports
leadReduction.status: FY2026 openings are delayed. The agency page includes mixed old and new instructions, so use only the current forms and status.
leadReduction.next: Check the live status before gathering the full application package.

healthyHomes.name: Healthy Homes
healthyHomes.desc: Provides home assessment, education, and referrals for certain asthma and indoor environmental concerns.
healthyHomes.why: May help a household understand triggers such as pests, moisture, smoke, or dust when a child has asthma or a pregnant person lives in the home.
prep: DC address and household contact information
The health concern and who is affected
Permission to assess the home and any useful medical or inspection information
healthyHomes.status: This is mainly assessment and referral, not a promise that every repair will be paid for. Confirm that intake is currently active.
healthyHomes.next: Check current intake before depending on this as a repair program.

floodsmart.name: FloodSmart Homes
floodsmart.desc: May provide a flood-resilience assessment, report, counseling, and an elevation certificate.
floodsmart.why: Useful for owners in mapped flood areas or homes with documented flooding concerns.
prep: Property address and ownership information
Past flooding records or photographs, if available
Access for the property assessment
floodsmart.status: The assessment does not mean construction work is automatically funded. Confirm current intake and later improvement assistance separately.
floodsmart.next: Start with the risk assessment before choosing flood work or insurance changes.

radon.name: Free Radon Test Kit
radon.org: DC Department of Energy and Environment
radon.desc: Provides DC residents with a test kit for an invisible radioactive gas linked to lung cancer.
radon.why: Testing is the only way to know whether radon may be elevated inside the home.
prep: A DC residential address
A suitable indoor testing location
Time to follow the kit instructions correctly
radon.status: The test is free. Any needed mitigation work is a separate service or cost.
radon.next: Order the kit and follow the placement and return instructions.

smoke.name: Free Smoke Alarm Service
smoke.org: DC Fire and Emergency Medical Services (FEMS)
smoke.desc: Provides a current official starting point for residents who need a working smoke alarm.
smoke.why: A missing or broken alarm is an immediate home-safety issue.
prep: DC residential address
Access to the home
Information about where alarms are missing or not working
smoke.status: Use the current FEMS service page because the request process may change.
smoke.next: Open the official service page and follow its current request instructions.

ddsCoord.name: Disability and family service coordination
ddsCoord.desc: A service coordinator or health-plan care manager can connect medical, school, benefits, transportation, and community supports.
ddsCoord.why: Useful when a family knows something is needed but does not know which housing, disability, health, or developmental program should start the process.
prep: Age and DC residency
Diagnosis, evaluation, or functional records
Medicaid, school, or provider information when applicable
ddsCoord.status: Service coordination does not automatically pay for construction. Home modifications must still meet the separate funding program’s rules.
ddsCoord.next: For a young child, check Strong Start. For Medicaid members, ask the health plan. Adults with developmental disabilities can check DDS.

beforeApply.title: Before applying for a rental
bullets: Ask for the written screening criteria before paying an application fee.
Confirm rent, deposit, utilities, move-in costs, and any refundable or nonrefundable fees.
Prepare identification, income documentation, rental history, and references that the property says it requires.
Never upload sensitive documents to this hub; complete applications only on a verified property or program website.
beforeApply.next: Write down the total move-in cost and required documents before you apply.

pet.title: Renting with a pet
bullets: Ask about limits on animal type, number, size, or breed.
Ask which charges are refundable, nonrefundable, or monthly.
Confirm vaccination, registration, or documentation requirements.
Assistance animals are not pets; different fair-housing rules may apply.
pet.next: Get the full pet policy and all animal-related charges in writing before applying.

insurance.title: Renters insurance
bullets: A landlord’s policy may not cover a renter’s belongings.
Compare personal-property, liability, temporary-living, and deductible terms.
Ask what losses or hazards are excluded.
Confirm whether the lease requires coverage and a minimum amount.
insurance.next: Compare coverage and exclusions, not only the monthly price.

guidance.title: Choosing human guidance
bullets: Housing counselors provide education in defined subject areas.
Program navigators may help only within a particular program or referral.
Locators, leasing professionals, and real-estate professionals may focus on market-rate rentals.
Ask whether the service is free, eligibility-based, referral-only, or fee-based.
guidance.next: Choose the type of help that matches your task, then review that provider’s services and terms.

cbo.title: Starting with a homeownership CBO
bullets: Many DC homebuyer programs direct applicants to participating community-based organizations.
A CBO may provide orientation, education, counseling, or program application guidance.
Participation does not guarantee program eligibility or mortgage approval.
Intake steps and appointment availability vary by organization.
cbo.next: Open the DHCD CBO directory, choose one participating organization, and follow its official orientation or intake instructions.

animals.title: Assistance animals and reasonable accommodations
bullets: An assistance animal is not the same as a pet.
A housing provider may have a process for requesting a reasonable accommodation.
Do not pay unofficial websites for certificates or registrations without checking official fair-housing guidance.
Individual rights and documentation questions may require qualified legal guidance.
animals.next: Review official housing-rights information before submitting an accommodation request.

unsafe.title: Unsafe housing conditions
bullets: Describe the problem to the housing provider in writing and keep a copy.
Save dated photos, messages, notices, and repair requests when safe to do so.
Review DC housing-code standards and the inspection process.
Seek qualified legal help if there is an eviction notice, court case, retaliation concern, or urgent legal issue.
unsafe.next: Create a dated record of the condition and open the official DOB inspection steps.

repair.title: Home-repair planning
bullets: Confirm whether a contractor and the work require District licenses or permits.
Get the scope, price, payment schedule, and warranty in writing.
Do not pay the full price before work begins without understanding the risk.
Check assistance-program eligibility before signing a contract if you may need financial help.
repair.next: Compare written estimates and verify required licenses or permits before agreeing to work.
